encounters.cc: Sudden red, itchy rash after starting new blood pressure medication

lines: Sudden red, itchy rash after starting new blood pressure medication
The patient is a 58-year-old male with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, coronary artery disease, and obesity presenting via telehealth for evaluation of a new rash.
He is followed longitudinally for chronic disease management with recent optimization of his diabetes and cardiovascular care.
He states that his home readings have also been consistently elevated.
To improve blood pressure control, a second antihypertensive agent is added to his regimen.
A few days later, while on vacation in Miami, he calls the clinic reporting the sudden appearance of a red, itchy rash and serous discharge from his nipples.
He says the rash is limited to areas exposed to the sun, including his face, neck, forearms, and hands.
He denies fever, recent illness, or use of new soaps or foods.
He also says he hasn't used sunscreen.
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus with established cardiovascular disease and obesity (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
He has a history of hypertension and hypercholesterolemia.
- Percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement (inferior wall)
- Incisional biopsy of tongue lesion (benign result, 1 year prior)
He currently takes simvastatin and lisinopril.
Smoking: Former smoker (40 pack-years), quit 5 years ago.
His blood pressure in the office is 160/100 mm Hg
On video consultation, an erythematous maculopapular rash with mild scaling is noted in sun-exposed areas.
The rest of his skin is unaffected.

encounters.cc: Diffuse muscle discomfort in thighs and shoulders for the past week

lines: Diffuse muscle discomfort in thighs and shoulders for the past week

The patient returns for evaluation of diffuse muscle discomfort in the context of longitudinal management for coronary artery disease and diabetes mellitus, with prior history of medication intolerance.
He describes a constant, dull pain in both thighs and shoulders that is aggravated by activity and does not improve with rest.
He has no recent history of trauma, infection, or new exercise routines.
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus with established cardiovascular disease and obesity (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
His past medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia.
- Percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement (inferior wall)
- Incisional biopsy of tongue lesion (benign result, 1 year prior)
His current medications are enalapril, aspirin, and a recently prescribed simvastatin, which was started 2 weeks ago after his last lipid profile review.
He does not use alcohol, illicit drugs, or herbal supplements.
He denies fever, rash, joint swelling, or sensory changes.
Physical examination is notable only for mild tenderness to palpation of proximal muscles without swelling, redness, or warmth.
Neurologic examination is normal, and there are no focal deficits.
Laboratory testing shows elevated creatine kinase levels, with normal renal function and electrolytes.

encounters.cc: Severe crushing chest pain radiating to left arm and jaw

lines: Severe crushing chest pain radiating to left arm and jaw

This 60-year-old male with coronary artery disease, Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity, previously evaluated for exertional chest discomfort in 2020, presents to the emergency department with severe chest pain that started 45 minutes ago while he was mowing the lawn.
The pain is described as a heavy pressure in the center of his chest, radiating to his left arm and jaw.
He also reports associated shortness of breath, nausea, and diaphoresis.
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus with established cardiovascular disease and obesity (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement (inferior wall)
- Incisional biopsy of tongue lesion (benign result, 1 year prior)
His medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin.
Smoking: Former smoker (40 pack-years), quit 5 years ago.
His blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg, heart rate is 98 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 94% on room air.
On examination, he is diaphoretic, anxious, and in obvious distress.
Cardiac examination reveals a regular rhythm without murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Lung fields are clear to auscultation bilaterally.

The ECG shows ST-segment elevations in leads II, III, and aVF.

lines: Sharp chest pain worsening with deep breaths and lying flat

encounters.cc: Persistent non-healing sore on tongue for two months

lines: Persistent non-healing sore on tongue for two months
Patient with CAD and diabetes presents with persistent oral lesion.
He denies any recent trauma to the area.
He reports that a similar lesion was biopsied one year ago and was benign.
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus with established cardiovascular disease and obesity (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, inferior wall (diagnosed 2024-01-15)
His medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with lisinopril, and hyperlipidemia, managed with atorvastatin.
- Percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement (inferior wall)
- Incisional biopsy of tongue lesion (benign result, 1 year prior)
On examination, you note a 1.5 cm white, thickened, non-removable plaque on the lateral border of his tongue.
The lesion is irregular in shape and has a slightly erythematous base.
